title: Tiling and Affinity Standup Notes — Priority Eviction & Batching Ideas (2026-12-09)
body:
Context: quick sync after the weekly runtime standup focused on an alternative to pure coalescing: "tiling + affinity" prioritization for batching and KV cache retention. The goal is to reduce p99 latency regressions for mid-length contexts (512-1024) while preserving throughput and lowering per-token cost for bursty traffic.

Summary of discussion:
- Problem: current coalescer combines requests aggressively which helps throughput but causes expensive KV cache churn for tails and causes kernel fallback thrashing under mixed sequence lengths. We see p99 spikes when a few long sequences enter a batch.
- Idea: tile incoming requests into small affinity buckets (by sequence-length band, requested model variant, and predicted reuse score) and drive batch formation from high-affinity tiles first. Separate low-affinity requests into opportunistic batches.
- Eviction concept: "eviction skyline" — assign each KV entry a two-part score: (recent_reuse_weighted_by_sequence_length, token_generation_cost_estimate). Eviction prefers removing entries with low reuse and high memory footprint per predicted future tokens. This biases retention toward small-but-hot prefixes that reduce latency for short completions.
- Kernel implications: encourage kernel selection that favors small-prefix fast-paths when a tile is dominated by short sequences, and keep large-sequence kernels isolated to their own tiles to avoid GLUE & kernel switching overhead in a single dispatch.

Decisions taken in the meeting:
- Prototype run: implement a proof-of-concept scheduler that creates 3 tiles per GPU: short (<=128), medium (129-1024), long (>1024). Within medium tile, sort by predicted reuse score (from recent KV hits per route).
- Start experiment on staging with mixed synthetic traffic and 10% shadow traffic for one dedicated shard. If staging looks good, we’ll A/B 5% production traffic next week.
- Rollback criteria: if p99 latency increases by >5% for any route or token cost increases by >3% for the A/B traffic in the first 6 hours.

Experiment plan (INF-4201):
- Implementation tasks:
  - Scheduler: Rajiv to add tiling layer and affinity scoring hook (PR branch: tiling-affinity-proto). Target: small internal PR by EOD 2026-12-13.
  - Eviction: Elena to prototype skyline score and integrate with Kafka-based cache-metrics sink for telemetry. Minimal impl in memstore with config flags. Target: 2026-12-15.
  - Kernel hints: Marcus to add heuristic flags to dispatcher so kernels can be hinted about tile characteristics (fast-prefix-prefer). Target: 2026-12-17.
- Metrics we will collect:
  - p50/p95/p99 latency per route and per tile
  - token/second and tokens-per-USD estimates
  - KV hit/miss rates and average KV entry lifetime per tile
  - GPU occupancy and kernel-switch counts per batch dispatch
- Success criteria:
  - p99 reduction of >=5% for short/medium routes under mixed load without throughput drop, or equivalent token-cost savings.

Open questions / risks:
- Memory fragmentation: tiling might leave long sequences pinned in a tile and starve memory for short sequences if not careful. Need eviction caps per tile.
- Estimating reuse: our proxy signal (recent KV hits) is noisy for cold-started routes; consider a lightweight ML model later but start with exponential smoothing.
- Kernel compatibility: some compressed-quantized kernels don't have the same fast-path behavior; ensure scheduler falls back gracefully.

Meeting notes (raw):
- Marcus: noted a production incident where a single long conversation caused kernel-switch thrash and P99 jump; tiling would have isolated that.
- Elena: suggested per-route retention caps and a cheap cost-estimator for token-expense to feed skyline scoring.
- Rajiv: prototype will reuse current coalescer internals, implementing tiling as a pre-filter; aim to keep changes minimal in serving-critical paths.
- Ivy: asked about rollout telemetry and alerted to include route-level anomaly detection to auto-fallback.

Action items (owner - due):
- Rajiv Menon - branch tiling-affinity-proto and PR for scheduler (2026-12-13)
- Elena Ortiz - skyline eviction prototype + telemetry writer (2026-12-15)
- Marcus Liu - dispatcher kernel-hint API doc + example (2026-12-17)
- Ivy Chen - test harness to simulate mixed sequence-length bursts and baseline replay (2026-12-14)
- Samantha Perez - write A/B plan and rollback runbook; coordinate with SRE for 5% traffic experiment (2026-12-16)

Follow-ups for next sync:
- Look at staging metrics after initial run (p50/p95/p99, KV hit rates) and decide whether to go to 5% A/B.
- If eviction skyline seems promising, run a microbenchmark measuring average KV entry cost and lifetime to tune skyline weights.
- Prepare a short demo for the weekly eng-all on 2026-12-22 if we have initial numbers.

Notes to self / rough ideas not discussed in meeting:
- Consider adding a per-tile early-exit for batches dominated by hallucination-prone prompts (detect via simple heuristics) to avoid wasting KV cache on low-quality prefixes.
- Explore a hybrid: tiled scheduling for latency-sensitive routes, classic coalescer for background bulk inference (embeddings, reranking).

Slack pointers and references:
- See thread: runtime-tiling (link above).
- Related infra ticket: INF-4177 (old prefetch experiments) may contain useful replay harnesses.

Status: keeping as draft until we have staging numbers. This doc will be iterated quickly; comments and suggestions welcome.
